prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematical analysis, with particular reference to: algebraic equations and inequalities, the study of a real-valued function, sequences and numerical series, limits of a real-valued function, continuity and differentiability of a real-valued function, fundamental theorems of differential calculus.

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding the terminology used in mathematical analysis.

Knowledge of the fundamental concepts of mathematical analysis (sequences and series of real-valued functions, real-valued functions of several variables, differential equations, multiple integrals, curves and curvilinear integrals, surfaces and surface integrals).
Knowing how to apply theorems and rules designed to solve problems.
Knowing how to consistently build some demonstrations.
Knowing how to build methods and procedures for the resolution of problems.
Knowing how to solve simple differential equations, multiple integrals, curvilinear and surface integrals, linear systems of equations.
Knowing how to identify the most appropriate methods to efficiently solve a mathematical problem, to be able to find some optimizations in the solving process of a mathematical problem.
Ability to work in groups, to orally present a topic related to mathematics.
The student has to develop the learning skills that will be necessary for inserting him in the following studies with a high autonomy of study, and critically face more general problems.

syllabus_topics: LIMITS AND CONTINUITY (FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VARIABLES)
PARTIAL AND DIRECTIONAL DERIVATIVES (FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VARIABLES)
MAIN THEOREMS (SCHWARZ, TOTAL DIFFERENTIAL, DERIVATION OF COMPOSITE FUNCTIONS)
PARTICULAR INTEGRAL AND GENERAL SOLUTION (ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS)
LOCAL AND GLOBAL EXISTENCE AND UNIQUENESS THEOREM
N-TH ORDER LINEAR DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS WITH CONSTANT COEFFICIENTS
CURVILINEAR INTEGRAL OF A LINEAR DIFFERENTIAL FORM
PROPERTIES (INTEGRALS OF FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VARIABLES)
APPLICATION TO AREAS AND VOLUMES (INTEGRALS OF FUNCTIONS OF SEVERAL VARIABLES)
AREA OF A SURFACE AND SURFACE INTEGRALS

assessment_methods.method: Written test: solving 4 problems, including parametric linear systems or matrix diagonalization, conic sections or analytical geometry, differential equations and/or Cauchy problems, extrema of a function in two variables, differential forms, curvilinear or surface integrals, multiple integrals.

Oral interview: evaluating knowledge of topics including definitions, theorem proofs, and exercise solving, specifically functions of two variables, differential equations, differential forms, integrals of functions of two variables.

assessment_rules: To pass the exam, both the written and oral tests must be passed. A minimum score of 18 on the written test is required to be admitted to the oral test. The final mark, expressed on a scale from 18 to 30 (possibly with laudem), depends on the written exam mark, with corrections based on the oral interview.
